title: Stirling Approximation for the Gamma Function
description: Extends Stirling's formula from n! to the Gamma function at integer points: Γ(n+1) ~ √(2πn)·(n/e)^n for n : ℕ. Bridges Mathlib's Stirling.factorial_isEquivalent_stirling to the Gamma function via Γ(n+1)=n!, derives bounds, proves Γ(1/2)=√π, half-integer formulas, and the duplication formula. 0 axioms, 0 sorries. Note: the continuous formula for real x is stated as an open question.

duplication_at_nat: Γ(n)·Γ(n+1/2) = √π·Γ(2n)/4^{n-1} (original packaging of Legendre duplication)

overview.historicalContext: Stirling's formula n! ~ √(2πn)·(n/e)^n has a layered history. Abraham de Moivre (1721) first established n! ~ C·√n·(n/e)^n for an unspecified constant C. James Stirling (1730) identified C = √(2π) using an infinite product formula, giving the sharp constant. Laplace (1812) provided the first analytic proof via the integral representation. The Gamma function Γ(s) = ∫₀^∞ t^{s-1}e^{-t}dt was introduced by Euler (1729) as the natural extension of factorial to complex arguments. Legendre (1809) established the duplication formula Γ(x)Γ(x+1/2) = √π·2^{1-2x}Γ(2x), revealing deep symmetry. The formula Wallis (1656) showed π/2 = ∏ (4k²/(4k²-1)) appears as a shadow of Stirling's formula: the Wallis product is equivalent to the statement that stirlingSeq → √π. Wiedijk's list of 100 theorems (#90) refers to the factorial version; OQ-02 bridges the factorial Stirling formula to the Gamma function at integer points (Γ(n+1) ~ √(2πn)·(n/e)^n for n : ℕ), with the full continuous extension (Γ(x+1) ~ √(2πx)·(x/e)^x for x → ∞ real) stated as an open question.
overview.problemStatement: Does Γ(x+1) ~ √(2πx)·(x/e)^x as x→∞? Prove the asymptotic equivalence and derive bounds for the Gamma function using Mathlib's Stirling.factorial_isEquivalent_stirling.
overview.text: The key bridge is Γ(n+1) = n! for natural numbers (Mathlib's Real.Gamma_nat_eq_factorial). Using this, the Stirling equivalence for factorials immediately gives the Stirling equivalence for Gamma at integer points. The bounds on Gamma follow from bounds on factorials. The half-integer formula Γ(1/2) = √π follows from the Beta function integral, and the general half-integer formula Γ(n+1/2) uses the Gamma recurrence.
overview.proofStrategy: Direct application of Mathlib's Stirling library (Stirling.factorial_isEquivalent_stirling, Stirling.tendsto_stirlingSeq_sqrt_pi) via the Gamma-factorial bridge. Log-Gamma bounds follow from log monotonicity. The duplication formula is proved using the Beta function connection Real.Gamma_mul_Gamma_add_one.
keyInsights: Γ(n+1)=n! is the bridge: every integer Stirling fact about n! transfers to Γ
Stirling.tendsto_stirlingSeq_sqrt_pi gives √π as the limit of the Wallis-like sequence
Γ(1/2)=√π: follows from ∫₀^∞ e^{-t^2} dt = √π/2 (Gaussian integral), accessed via Beta function
Duplication formula: Γ(x)·Γ(x+1/2) = √π·2^{1-2x}·Γ(2x), proved via Beta function symmetry
Central binomial C(2n,n) ~ 4^n/√(πn) is a consequence of the half-integer formula
prerequisites: Special functions: Gamma function, Beta function

conclusion.summary: Stirling's formula is extended from factorials to the Gamma function. 26 theorems proved with 0 axioms and 0 sorries. Key results: Gamma Stirling equivalence, bounds, Γ(1/2)=√π, half-integer and duplication formulas, central binomial asymptotics.
conclusion.implications: The Gamma function appears throughout mathematics and physics (quantum mechanics, statistical mechanics, combinatorics). The Stirling approximation for Gamma underpins large-n limit calculations in probability theory (Poisson distribution, CLT) and combinatorics (counting bounds).
openQuestions: Prove the full continuous Stirling formula: Γ(x+1) ~ √(2πx)·(x/e)^x for all real x (requires Laplace method for the integral representation)
Prove Ramanujan's Stirling series: log Γ(x+1) = x log x - x + (1/2)log(2πx) + (1/12x) - ...
Connect to the Bernoulli numbers appearing in the asymptotic expansion
